categories.name: Upscaling and super resolution
categories.description: Resize an image using interpolation, edge reconstruction, or temporal upscaling.

subcategories.name: General purpose
subcategories.description: For photos, video, games, and interfaces; compare definition, halos, and processing cost.

subcategories.name: Anime and line art
subcategories.description: For animation and visual novels; compare outlines, flat colors, and fine textures.

subcategories.name: Pixel art
subcategories.description: Choose intact pixel blocks or smoother outlines; integer scales help maintain an even grid.

subcategories.name: Temporal reconstruction
subcategories.description: Reconstruct detail from captured-frame history; limited motion and depth information requires checking ghosting, occlusion, and UI.

subcategories.name: Downscaling and resizing
subcategories.description: For downscaling or fitting the final size after a fixed-scale upscaler.

categories.name: Cleanup and restoration
categories.description: Reduce noise, banding, or line defects, usually before upscaling and sharpening.

subcategories.name: Denoising
subcategories.description: Start with low strength and compare noise reduction against lost fine texture.

subcategories.name: Debanding
subcategories.description: Smooth gradients in skies and shadows without erasing real texture.

subcategories.name: Line restoration
subcategories.description: Refine animation outlines or line thickness, usually before the main upscaler.

categories.name: Anti-aliasing
categories.description: Smooth jagged edges using the current frame or captured-frame history.

subcategories.name: Spatial
subcategories.description: Process edges in the current frame; check for softened text and thin lines.

subcategories.name: Temporal
subcategories.description: Experimental processing with captured-frame history; check ghosting and thin-line stability.

categories.name: Sharpening
categories.description: Enhance local contrast and edge definition; watch for halos and amplified noise.

subcategories.name: General sharpening
subcategories.description: Usually apply after scaling; start with one sharpener to avoid stacking halos and noise.

categories.name: Frame generation and frame rate
categories.description: Generate intermediate frames or limit the base frame rate alongside Frame rate and refresh settings.

subcategories.name: Frame generation
subcategories.description: Use one frame generator per group; higher displayed FPS does not raise the game simulation rate.

subcategories.name: Frame-rate control
subcategories.description: Limit the capture and processing base rate; moving the entry does not change its scope.

categories.name: Display styles
categories.description: Adjust colors, brightness, textures, or retro display style to suit your preferences.

subcategories.name: CRT
subcategories.description: Retro scanlines, masks, glow, and curvature, usually applied after scaling.

subcategories.name: Image adjustment
subcategories.description: Adjust brightness and color to taste; check HDR highlights and gradients.

subcategories.name: AI image enhancement
subcategories.description: Reshape textures and detail for advanced users willing to compare against the original.

categories.name: Diagnostics
categories.description: Inspect estimated motion and confidence to diagnose temporal processing.

subcategories.name: Diagnostics
subcategories.description: View motion and confidence; diagnostic maps are not normal viewing output.

categories.name: HDR components
categories.description: Convert between HDR and SDR, or expand SDR images into HDR.

effects.name: XeSS SR
effects.summary: XeSS temporal upscaling from captured frames.
effects.details:
Supports 1×–3× per axis, requiring an available XeSS runtime and a supported GPU.

Use as the main upscaler, followed by gentle sharpening if needed. Motion is estimated from captured images without true game depth, so results differ from in-game integration. Check fast motion, occlusion, and HUD elements.

Optical-flow method and quality affect processing cost and require restarting scaling after changes. Compare highlights and colors in HDR.

effects.name: XeSS_FrameGeneration
effects.details:
Defaults to 2× with AMD optical flow at Quality. Requires the bundled XeSSFG runtime and a supported GPU; use one frame generator per group.

3×/4× on non-Intel GPUs uses this project’s experimental compatibility path and matching bundled runtime; it is outside Intel’s official multiframe support. Use no optical flow or AMD optical flow for 3×/4×; NVIDIA optical flow is currently for 2×.

Set base FPS under Frame rate and refresh. Generation runs after image processing regardless of list position and does not raise game simulation FPS. Check motion, occlusion, HUD, cursor, and HDR colors. Multiplier and optical-flow changes require restarting scaling.

effects.name: RTXVideo_Denoise
effects.summary: AI video denoising with four strength levels.
effects.details:
For video with grain or compression noise. Keeps the input size and usually runs before upscaling. Low/Medium/High/Ultra are processing levels; start at Medium and compare texture and noise.

Requires a supported NVIDIA RTX GPU, driver, and bundled Video Effects runtime. Higher strength is not always a better match. HDR uses SDR-compatible mapping and quantization, so inspect highlights and color. Strength updates live; preparing the new model may temporarily add overhead.

effects.name: HDR → SDR
effects.summary: Map HDR for SDR processing or display.
effects.details:
Keeps the input size and runs before effects requiring SDR. Compatibility-pair mode reserves highlight range; the later SDR → HDR entry inherits paired settings. SDR-display mode is for direct viewing.

Enable Windows HDR on the source display and use Graphics Capture. The paired intermediate differs from ordinary SDR; quantization, clipping, and processing can lose highlights or color, and restoration is not lossless. Parameter changes require restarting scaling.

effects.summary: Expand SDR into HDR using NVIDIA AI.
